newsitem.title: UK: OPEC hits 26.4 mbpd in Dec as Iraq returns-survey.
newsitem.headline: OPEC hits 26.4 mbpd in Dec as Iraq returns-survey.

text.p: OPEC output rose again in December, boosted by Iraq's return to the international market for the first time in six years and extra output from new fields in a number of other member countries.

Wellhead crude oil production from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries rose 360,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.40 million from a revised 26.04 million in November, a Reuter survey of oil analysts, OPEC delegates and company officials found.
Most OPEC countries continued to ignore their increasingly irrelevant output quotas at a time when winter demand has easily absorbed rising supplies and kept crude prices near six year highs.
"If OPEC is overproducing then it is necessary to meet demand," said Oystein Berentsen, head of international crude trading at Norwegian oil producing giant Statoil, on Thursday.
OPEC's official output ceiling is a combined 25.033 million bpd.
The 11-member cartel is pumping 1.3 million bpd more than a year ago.
Only a trio of core Middle East OPEC members -- Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait -- continue to keep extra capacity in mothballs.

"Most of OPEC's non-core members are pursuing capacity expansion plans in 1997 and on present evidence can be expected to utilise that capacity once it is installed," said London's Centre for Global Energy Studies.

Iraq found no trouble in marketing its first exports under the United Nations' oil-for-food exchange which permits $2 billion of sales over six months under strict U.N. supervision, industry monitors said.
A U.N. overseers report said Iraq had exported 10.7 million barrels in nine cargoes by January 3, most from its Turkish Mediterranean pipeline outlet at Ceyhan.
Iraqi exports, beginning from Ceyhan on December 16, were estimated at 560,000 bpd on average for the second half of December.
Given domestic consumption and small sales to Jordan at a combined 650,000 bpd, Iraqi output for December averaged 930,000 bpd, industry monitors said.
Small volumes of extra production from new oilfields in Qatar, Libya, Algeria and Nigeria operated by foreign companies also were spotted by industry monitors.
Qatar's new al-Rayyan field was averaging 32,000 bpd by early January, Gulf industry officials said, helping carry OPEC's smallest producer to 520,000 bpd, almost 40 percent over quota.

Canada's Abacan Resources brought Nigeria's NGO field onstream in mid-December at about 20,000 bpd, tweaking the West African producer up to 2.06 million. NGO is expected to hit a full 50,000 bpd in January.
In Libya, Spain's Repsol began 20,000 bpd of output in mid December from the Murzuk field, aiming for 45,000 bpd early this year.
Venezuela showed no sign of diverting from its upward course, again pumping at some 3.15 million bpd in December, well above its 2.36 million bpd quota.
State company PdVSA plans raising output to 3.416 million bpd on average this year including 355,000 bpd earmarked for domestic consumption, according to estimates provided to the government.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
